name: Outer Space (Crayola)
lede: Outer Space is a Crayola crayon, a near-black blue-grey named for the dark of space rather than for any pigment.

sections.title: Where the name comes from
sections.body: Outer Space is listed among Crayola's named crayons, with no coiner or year attached in the sources checked here, so the exact date it entered the box is undocumented [1]. The name reads plainly: it names the color of space itself, the way Crayola also names crayons after fruit or weather [1]. Its nearest named neighbor is [[gunmetal]], only 2.5 units off on screen, with [[black-grey]] and [[pale-gunmetal]] close behind [2].

sections.title: A Japanese neighbor, unrelated
sections.body: Our library also files this swatch under *Tetsuonando*, "iron storage," a traditional Japanese color name with its own separate record [1]. The two names share only the hex value; nothing ties the Crayola crayon to the Japanese dye tradition [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a color within range of this swatch in 702 of 23,781 paintings, 2.95 percent, as photographed; narrowing to at least five percent of the canvas leaves 416 [3]. That makes it more common than 81 percent of the named colors in our library [3]. It most often plays a mid-tone, in 49 percent of those 416 paintings by lightness rank, so varnish cannot fake the result [3].

Fra Angelico is its most devoted painter, present in 4 of his 16 works here, 5.1 times the rate expected from the museums those paintings come from [3]. The earliest match dates to 1099, centuries before any crayon existed, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
